2608.30884.title: Evaluating and Mitigating Anti-LGBTQ Biases in German and Multilingual Language Models
2608.30884.paper_summary: While gender and racial biases in language models have been widely studied, anti-LGBTQ biases remain underexplored, particularly beyond English. Existing benchmarks often do not capture cultural and linguistic variation and rely on gender representations. This paper introduces a multilingual German-English benchmark dataset for the evaluation of anti-LGBTQ biases in language models. It combines community-sourced stereotypes from German-speaking queer individuals with a German translation of WinoQueer. The data is used to evaluate eight language models across sizes and architectures and explore mitigation through fine-tuning on community and progressive media content. Results show that language models reproduce anti-queer stereotypes, with variation across identities and models. Differences between the translated and community-based data highlight the importance of cultural adaptation for multilingual bias evaluation. Fine-tuning reduces bias on average, but not consistently across models and identities. Warning: This text contains examples of anti-queer hateful language and stereotypes.
2608.30884.paper_summary_zh: 雖然性別和種族偏見在語言模型中已被廣泛研究，但反LGBTQ偏見仍然未被充分探討，特別是在英語以外的語言中。現有的基準往往無法捕捉文化和語言的變異，並依賴性別表徵。本文介紹了一個多語言的德英基準數據集，用於評估語言模型中的反LGBTQ偏見。它結合了來自德語社群的刻板印象和WinoQueer的德語翻譯。這些數據用於評估八種不同大小和架構的語言模型，並探索通過在社群和進步媒體內容上進行微調來減輕偏見。結果顯示，語言模型重現了反酷兒的刻板印象，並在身份和模型之間存在變異。翻譯數據與社群數據之間的差異突顯了文化適應在多語言偏見評估中的重要性。微調平均上減少了偏見，但在模型和身份之間並不一致。警告：本文包含反酷兒仇恨語言和刻板印象的例子。
2608.30884.author: Melina Morch et.al.
